target: MJ-PR-004 P0 service startup and local persistence; MJ-REQ-012, MJ-REQ-013, MJ-REQ-014
action: Diagnose Docker Desktop relaunch, repair the existing MJobs project without replacing its volumes, and verify the Compose restart-policy change in an isolated personal project

observations.before: After Docker Desktop relaunched, postgres and redis were exited with restart=no; API and three workers were restarting or unready because their dependencies were absent.
observations.observed: Both existing dependency containers were started in place and changed from restart=no to restart=unless-stopped. API readiness returned HTTP 200 with database, queue, worker and mock checks true. No named volume was replaced or deleted.

commands: docker inspect restart policies for postgres, redis, API and three workers
PUT /profiles with labeled synthetic test-only profile pr004-restart-probe
docker compose -p mjobs-pr004-20260930 stop api worker source-worker document-worker postgres redis
observations.observed: First run created an ignored local .env without printing its secret, applied migrations and reached readiness. All six long-running containers carried restart=unless-stopped. The personal browser/API probe passed with fictional actions rejected and external submission disabled. After a complete controlled service stop and relaunch, the synthetic profile remained readable; database, queue and worker checks were true and external submission remained false.

local_tests.observed: 14 tests passed in 5.790 seconds; restart-policy test first failed for postgres and redis before the Compose change

migration_data_impact: No schema migration or existing business-row change. The live mjobs project retained its original volumes. The isolated project uses separately named volumes and a synthetic test-only profile.
cleanup: docker compose -p mjobs-pr004-20260930 down removed only the isolated project's containers and networks; its three named test volumes were retained. After the isolated build, docker compose build --quiet api in clean main restored the shared mjobs-local:spine tag to main's source (main_contract_search=False). The existing mjobs project still returned HTTP 200 readiness with all four checks true.
rollback_recovery: For a code rollback, revert the two Compose restart lines; existing data volumes remain. The live Docker policy adjustment is reversible with docker update --restart no on the two verified mjobs dependency containers, but reverting it would reproduce the relaunch failure until the Compose change is deployed.
limitations: No Docker Desktop or host daemon restart was performed by this test; runtime inspection and controlled service stop/relaunch prove the configured policy and volume persistence, not a full host-reboot test.
Backup and restore commands, uploaded resume persistence, and complete raw docker compose first-run acceptance remain open; MJ-REQ-013 and MJ-REQ-014 are PARTIAL.
The live mjobs project uses its existing main checkout configuration; the PR code change must be integrated to persist the policy through future Compose reconciliation.
